contexts.text: Some whole period is designated in the Word by either day, week, month, or year; even if it were one of a hundred or a thousand years; like the days in , by which are signified the periods of the regeneration of the man of the Most Ancient Church...

Thus by a year, as also by a day, and a week, is signified an entire period, less or greater, of fewer or of more years; nay, a period abstractedly... Here... the second period of the Church is signified, which was when this second Church began.

A week = an entire period of any state or time; as of reformation, of regeneration, of temptation; both of a man in particular, and of the Church in general. Thus, a period, whether it be of a thousand years, of a hundred, or of ten, or of as many days, hours, minutes, and so on, is called a week. AC 2213:end.
A year = an entire period of the Church, from beginning to end... Illustrated.
An entire period of the Church, or the time of its duration. Signified.
The reason a week, etc., = a state, and also a period, is that all states have also their periods; that is, their beginning, successive, and end...
The first period... Signified, Explained.
In the following things of this period.
Three = one period and its Continuous from beginning to end. AE 532:2.
When man is being regenerated, the periods of the first state are from the truths of faith to the goods of charity... These periods last until the man has been regenerated. Explained.
Seventy involves the same as seven (which) = an entire period from beginning to end; thus a full state. Illustrated. AC 9228, Illustrated. AE 20.
The entire period before the Lord would come. Signified.
The entire period of this state. Signified.
That the sphere of the love of procreating... makes periods, by means of which creation is preserved... Explained.
In life's first period...

For there are four periods of life through which man passes, from infancy to old age. Enumerated... But these periods of life are the periods of the life of the spirit of man, and not in like manner of his body...
All these are alternate consummations which are natural and temporary, but still are periodical...
Three years = an entire period from beginning to end; thus total destruction. AE 532:6.
Forty days = an entire period, and the duration of temptations... ( = the entire period of the vastation of the Church. AE 654:53.)
God. 7. 3. These progressions of ends... go and return by periods, which are called the circles of Things.
Summaries 4. The periodical changes in the Most Ancient Church are described in the first chapters of Genesis...
[5]. The periodical changes of state in the Ancient Church are described in Genesis...
[6]. The periodical changes in the Israelitish Church are described in (the historical and prophetical books).
[7]. The periodical changes in the Christian Church are described in both Testaments...
That of each Church there have been four successive states, or periods, which are meant by morning, day, evening, and night. General article.
